description: Tier-based fault tolerance experiments for Bitcoin network resilience analysis
purpose: Systematic analysis of crash impacts, stress conditions, and block interval effects. Crashes happen DURING observation window for comparable metrics.
total_duration_estimate: ~43 hours for full suite (4 runs each = 224 total runs, observe_s=600)

baseline.name: Baseline (No Faults)
baseline.description: Perfect conditions - establish performance baseline with 128 nodes. Uses Shifted Exponential Distribution (min_interval=2.0s) to prevent fork-causing race conditions while maintaining realistic block time variance.

analysis_comparisons.name: Tier A: Crash Impact Isolation
hypotheses: Higher crash_fraction leads to increased latency and reduced throughput
Simultaneous crashes cause sharper performance degradation than sequential
Extended downtime (120s) allows clear observation of crash impact on recovery metrics
Fast resync reduces recovery time compared to full resync
Longer crash duration (180s vs 90s) leads to more missed blocks and longer recovery time

analysis_comparisons.name: Tier B: Stress Environment Analysis
hypotheses: Poor network conditions amplify crash impact on recovery
High transaction load increases mempool congestion during recovery
Fast resync provides greater benefits under stress conditions
Omission faults alone (without crashes) cause measurable performance degradation
Packet loss has different impact than high latency on confirmation times
Combined omission faults (loss + latency) have synergistic effects
Partial network faults (affecting subset of nodes) cause different degradation patterns than global faults
Regional network problems (25-50% nodes) are more realistic than global network failures
Network partition effects differ from uniform network degradation across all nodes

analysis_comparisons.name: Tier C: Block Interval Sensitivity
hypotheses: Fast block intervals (6s) increase fork rate but reduce confirmation latency
Standard block intervals (12s) provide baseline recovery behavior
Slower block intervals (24s) provide more stable recovery but longer confirmation times
Fast resync benefits are more pronounced with standard block intervals

analysis_comparisons.name: Cross-Tier: Recovery Mode Comparison
hypotheses: Fast resync consistently reduces recovery time across all conditions
Full resync provides better chain validation but at performance cost

analysis_comparisons.name: Tier D: Network Size Comparison (64 vs 128 nodes)
hypotheses: Larger networks (128 nodes) have longer block propagation times
Recovery time scales with network size due to more nodes syncing
Crash impact is similar at same crash_fraction regardless of absolute node count
Staggered crashes affect smaller networks differently due to fewer remaining nodes
Network stress compounds with network size effects

analysis_comparisons.name: Tier E: High Load (20 tx/s) Analysis
hypotheses: Higher transaction load increases confirmation latency under all conditions
Crash recovery is slower under high load due to mempool backlog
High load amplifies the difference between full_resync and fast_resync
Network degradation has more severe impact at high load
Availability may decrease at high load if blocks cannot keep up with submissions
